title: India Come From Behind to Beat Japan 4-1, Win Sixth Asian Champions Trophy
excerpt: Trailing from the third minute in Mohali, India equalised through Shilanand Lakra in the 42nd minute and scored three times in the final quarter to complete a hat-trick of titles.
body:
• India beat Japan 4-1 in the Men's Asian Champions Trophy final in Mohali on Thursday, November 5, 2026, to win the title for a record sixth time.
  • Japan led from the third minute through Kazumasa Matsumoto; Shilanand Lakra equalised in the 42nd minute before India scored three times in the final quarter.
  • The win makes India the first team to complete a hat-trick of Asian Champions Trophy titles, according to reports of the final.
  • India reached the final unbeaten, thrashing South Korea 8-1 in the semi-final after also beating Japan 4-1 in the league stage.

India came from a goal down to beat Japan 4-1 in the final of the Men's Asian Champions Trophy 2026 in Mohali on Thursday and lift the trophy for a record sixth time. Japan struck first, and for long stretches the hosts were chasing the game. The equaliser arrived late in the third quarter, and the match turned decisively in the final quarter, when India scored three times to pull away.

How the final turned

Japan took the lead in the third minute through Kazumasa Matsumoto, the earliest possible statement that this would not be a repeat of the league-stage meeting between the sides. India pressed but could not find a way through before half-time, and the score stayed 1-0 deep into the match.

The breakthrough came in the 42nd minute, when Shilanand Lakra equalised. With the scores level, India raised the tempo in the final quarter and scored three more goals to seal a 4-1 win and, with it, a hat-trick of Asian Champions Trophy titles — a first for any team in the tournament, according to reports of the final. Malaysia finished third in the tournament.

The road to the title

India, coached by Craig Fulton, arrived at the title match at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali unbeaten, with six wins from six matches. In the semi-finals, the hosts thrashed South Korea 8-1, while Japan overcame Malaysia on penalties after a goalless draw in regulation time to reach their third final, having finished runners-up in 2013 and 2021.

The final was the second 4-1 scoreline between these teams in this tournament. In the league stage in Jalandhar, India beat Japan by the same margin: Abhishek scored twice in his 150th international match, captain Harmanpreet Singh converted a penalty corner and Vishnu Kant Singh added the fourth, after Shota Yamada had equalised from a penalty stroke. That result booked India's semi-final place and set the pattern this side has followed all tournament — absorb early pressure, then score in clusters late on.

What it means

India went into the final as two-time defending champions and five-time winners overall, the most successful team in the tournament's history. A sixth crown, won at home in Punjab after trailing in the final, extends that record and keeps the title in India for a third straight edition. Japan, beaten finalists for a third time, leave with the consolation of having pushed the hosts harder than any side managed earlier in the tournament — they led this final for 39 minutes before Lakra's equaliser changed it.

For followers watching from abroad, the full final report is available from Khel Now's coverage of the tournament, which tracked India's unbeaten run through the Punjab event.
